content.title: About
content.content: Strawberry cake or cupcake is a tender baked dessert that combines juicy pieces of fresh or frozen strawberries with a soft batter. Depending on the recipe, it may be topped with buttercream, glaze, or dusted with powdered sugar. This treat is popular both in cafés and home kitchens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Strawberries provide more than 150% of the daily recommended vitamin C per 100 g.
Traditional cupcakes are often leavened with baking powder rather than yeast, giving them a denser crumb than sponge cakes.
The pairing of strawberry and whipped cream is a classic in European pastry tradition.
In the United States, strawberry cupcakes are a common feature at summer picnics and barbecues.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Strawberries offer antioxidant protection and support the immune system.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many cakes, a strawberry‑flavored cupcake typically contains less saturated fat when heavy frosting is omitted.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Strawberry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to strawberries, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Cakes and cupcakes often contain added sugar, which can be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching calorie intake.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: When using pre‑made mixes, artificial flavors and preservatives may be present.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Strawberry cake or cupcake can be served as a standalone dessert, sliced into portions, and garnished with fresh berries and mint. It pairs well with tea, coffee, or a light dessert wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished cake or cupcake in the refrigerator, covered with plastic wrap or in an airtight container, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 2 months; thaw in the refrigerator before serving.

cereal-or-granola-bar-with-nuts-chocolat.title: Cereal or granola bar with nuts, chocolate coated

content.title: About
content.content: A cereal or granola bar with nuts, chocolate coated combines whole grains, a mix of nuts (almonds, walnuts, hazelnuts, etc.) and a sweet chocolate glaze. It is a convenient on‑the‑go snack that provides energy and a range of nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Granola originated in the United States in the early 1900s as a healthier alternative to biscuits.
The chocolate coating often contains cocoa butter, giving the bar a glossy, crisp finish.
Nuts are usually roasted, which enhances their aroma and increases the content of healthy fats.
Many variations exist: with dried fruit, seeds, honey, or added protein powders.
These bars are popular in sports nutrition because of their high carbohydrate and protein content.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Complex carbs from the grains together with quick sugars from the chocolate provide an immediate and sustained energy boost.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The bar contains vitamin E, magnesium, iron and zinc, which support immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Grains and nuts add fiber that promotes regular digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in the chocolate glaze provides polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: Bars containing nuts can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to tree nuts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The chocolate coating adds simple sugars, which may be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: These bars are calorie‑dense; portion size should be moderate, especially for sedentary lifestyles.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some manufacturers use partially hydrogenated oils in the glaze; choose versions that are free of trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar can be eaten straight from the wrapper as a quick snack, chopped into yogurt or kefir, or sprinkled over oatmeal. It can also be broken into pieces and used as a topping for desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bars in a cool, dry place, preferably in the original packaging or an airtight container. For longer storage (over 3 months) keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the chocolate coating from melting.

content.title: About
content.content: Tequila Sunrise is a classic cocktail made with tequila, orange juice, and grenadine. It gets its name from the striking gradient of color—from deep red at the bottom to golden at the top—resembling a sunrise.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink was created in the 1930s in California and quickly became popular across the United States.
It is traditionally served in a tall highball glass over ice.
Grenadine adds both sweetness and the characteristic sunrise hue.
One story says the name comes from the habit of drinking it at dawn after late‑night parties.
Tequila Sunrise is often featured in bartending competitions as an example of a perfect color gradient.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Orange juice is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Antioxidants in grenadine
items.content: Grenadine, made from pomegranate juice, provides polyphenols with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Moderate tequila intake
items.content: In small amounts, ethanol can promote vasodilation and improve circulation.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Tequila Sunrise contains alcohol and should only be consumed by individuals of legal drinking age.

items.title: Sugar in grenadine
items.content: Grenadine often has a high sugar content, which can be problematic for people with diabetes or weight concerns.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Orange juice may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Pour 45 ml tequila into a glass filled with ice, add 90 ml fresh orange juice, then gently drizzle 15 ml grenadine so it settles at the bottom. Do not stir, preserving the gradient. Garnish with an orange slice or a cherry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tequila in a cool, dark place with the bottle tightly sealed. Fresh orange juice is best used immediately, but if refrigerated it stays fresh for up to 3 days. Grenadine can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 6 months.
